title: Bucatini Cacio e Pepe
subtitle: Thick hollow pasta with pecorino and black pepper
excerpt: Bucatini tossed with a silky sauce of pecorino romano and generous black pepper. Only three core ingredients, but technique matters. The sauce must emulsify without seizing.
sourceNotes: Roman pasta dish. Bucatini is used here in place of tonnarelli for wider availability; pecorino romano is the canonical cheese.

content.text: Cacio e pepe has only three real ingredients: pasta, cheese, and pepper. The challenge is getting the cheese to melt into a sauce rather than clump. Use starchy pasta water and keep the heat low when you add the cheese.
Bring a large pot of water to the boil. Use less water than normal: a smaller volume makes starchier pasta water. Add salt and cook the bucatini until al dente.
While the pasta cooks, toast the cracked pepper in a dry wide frying pan over a medium heat for 1 minute until fragrant. Remove from the heat.
Mix the grated pecorino and parmesan together in a bowl. Add 3 tablespoons of hot pasta water. Stir to form a thick paste. It should be smooth, not grainy.
Reserve 200ml of pasta water. Drain the bucatini. Add it straight to the frying pan with the pepper over a low heat.
Add 80ml of pasta water to the pan. Toss the pasta vigorously for 1 minute so it absorbs the starchy water.
Remove the pan from the heat. Add the cheese paste and toss quickly. Add pasta water a tablespoon at a time until the sauce is glossy and coats the pasta. Work fast.
Serve immediately. Finish each bowl with an extra grind of black pepper.

items.symptom: The cheese has clumped into rubbery lumps.
items.cause: The pan was too hot when the cheese paste was added.
items.fix: Always take the pan off the heat before adding the cheese. The residual heat from the pasta is enough to melt it.

items.symptom: The sauce is too thick and pasty.
items.cause: Not enough pasta water was added when tossing.
items.fix: Add pasta water a tablespoon at a time while tossing until the sauce loosens to a silky consistency.

items.symptom: The pepper is too sharp and raw-tasting.
items.cause: The pepper was not toasted before use.
items.fix: A 1-minute dry toast in the pan mellows the heat and brings out the aromatic notes. Do not skip this step.
